title: First Mexican Empire
capsule: The First Mexican Empire was declared on 19 May 1822 when the congress acclaimed Agustín de Iturbide, architect of Mexican independence via the Plan of Iguala (1821), as Emperor Agustín I. At its greatest extent the empire encompassed all of former New Spain including Central America as far as present-day Costa Rica, though the Central American provinces seceded in July 1823. Fiscal insolvency and Iturbide's dissolution of congress in October 1822 provoked republican opposition led by Antonio López de Santa Anna; Iturbide abdicated on 19 March 1823 and went into exile, and the empire was dissolved in favor of a federal republic on 1 November 1823.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial claims of the First Mexican Empire are documented from administrative records of New Spain, but effective control over peripheral regions (Yucatán, Central America) was limited; frontier extents are approximate.
